prompt: According to IAS 38 regarding the accounting for research and development costs it is CORRECT to say that …

options.text: Research and development costs have to be recognised as intangible assets if certain criteria of IAS 38 are met
Research costs have to be expensed; development costs have to be recognised as an intangible asset if the criteria of IAS 38 are met
Research and development costs have to be expensed regardless of the criteria of IAS 38
Research costs have to be recognised as intangible assets if certain criteria are met and development costs have to be expensed

explanation: Research never meets the recognition criteria (future benefits cannot be demonstrated) → expense. Development costs MUST be capitalised once all IAS 38 criteria are met (exam 2019 and 2024).

prompt: In which statement of Lumen Games can you find the staff costs expensed? Indicate the amount.
modelAnswer: Not on the face of the income statement: Lumen presents expenses by FUNCTION (cost of sales, R&D, selling, G&A), so staff costs are spread across these lines. They are disclosed in the notes (Note 7): 1,050 M€ (wages 820 + social charges 230). Under the function method IAS 1 requires such nature information in the notes.
keyPoints: Income statement is by function → staff costs not visible as a line

prompt: Was there a cash capital increase in N? If yes, specify its terms (increase in share capital, share premium, cash received, number of shares).
modelAnswer: Yes. Share capital rose from 13.0 to 15.4 (+2.4 M€) and share premium from 1,090.0 to 1,207.6 (+117.6 M€); the cash flow statement shows 'Proceeds from capital increase' of 120 M€ = 2.4 + 117.6. With a par value of €0.10, 24 million new shares were issued at an average price of €5.00 (120 / 24).

prompt: Explain why 'depreciation, amortisation, provisions' appears as a positive amount in the statement of cash flows.
modelAnswer: Lumen uses the indirect method: operating cash flow starts from net income and adds back expenses that did not cause a cash outflow. Depreciation, amortisation (e.g. of capitalised game development costs) and additions to provisions reduced net income by 900 M€ but no cash left the company in N, so they are added back (positive amount).
keyPoints: Indirect method starts from net income
They are added back to reconcile to operating cash flow

prompt: Does Lumen have significant influence over any associates? List all items in the financial statements that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Yes. Balance sheet: 'Investments in associates' 35 (31 in N−1) – the equity method is used for entities under significant influence. Income statement: 'Share of profit of associates' 4. Cash flow statement: 'Share of profit of associates, net of dividends' (−4) is deducted because it is a non-cash income.
keyPoints: Adjustment in the cash flow statement

prompt: Are all Lumen subsidiaries 100% owned? Justify your answer.
modelAnswer: No. The balance sheet shows non-controlling interests of 12 (11 in N−1) in equity, and the income statement attributes 1 of net income to non-controlling interests. NCI only exist if minority shareholders hold part of at least one fully consolidated subsidiary.

prompt: Does Lumen use leasing to finance any of its assets? List all items that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Yes. Balance sheet: right-of-use assets 180 and lease liabilities 195 (IFRS 16). Income statement: interest on lease liabilities (9) within financial expense (depreciation of ROU assets within the functional lines). Cash flow statement: 'Repayment of lease liabilities' (40) in financing activities.
keyPoints: Interest on lease liabilities / repayment of lease liabilities

prompt: Do you think Lumen made new (small) acquisitions in N? List all items that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Yes, most likely small ones. The cash flow statement shows 'Acquisition of subsidiaries, net of cash acquired' (18), and goodwill increased from 230 to 241 (+11) – goodwill is not amortised, so an increase points to new business combinations (or currency effects). The amounts are small compared with the group's size.
keyPoints: Cash outflow for acquisition of subsidiaries (18)
Goodwill not amortised → increase from acquisitions
